comments.note: I don't know what demoed means in the condensed or the original version but at least you can tell the there is a Sister and a hospital so perhaps it's about the hospital closing. Also, the dialog is confused since it's presented as said by Tommy but Tuppence says some of it.
comments.author: Tom
comments.paragraph: Tommy chuckled. "Good old hospital—demobbed like everything else, I suppose?"

comments.note: Not clear that Tuppence is the speaker.
comments.author: Tom
comments.paragraph: Tuppence sighed. "Yes. You too?" Tommy nodded. "Two months ago."

comments.note: This misses the reference to her working in the officers hospital which  provides the context for her duties
comments.author: Tom
comments.paragraph: They found a table. "Funny scraps one does overhear," murmured Tommy. "I passed two Johnnies in the street to-day talking about some one called Jane Finn. Did you ever hear such a name?"

comments.note: Not clear Tommy is the speaker.
comments.author: Tom
comments.paragraph: Tommy was pleasantly ugly, with a shock of slicked-back red hair—nondescript, yet unmistakably the face of a gentleman and a sportsman. Tuppence had no claim to beauty, but there was character and charm in the elfin lines of her little face, with its determined chin and large, wide-apart grey eyes. She wore a small bright green toque over her bobbed black hair; her appearance was a valiant attempt at smartness.

comments.author: Tom
comments.paragraph: "Very well." Tuppence helped herself liberally to buttered toast and gave the abridged biography of Miss Prudence Cowley, fifth daughter of Archdeacon Cowley of Little Missendell, Suffolk: she had entered an officers' hospital, where her duties ran from plate-washing and peeling potatoes to sweeping out wards (where she found a friend of her childhood in Lieutenant Thomas Beresford—bow, Tommy!), then a trade van, a motor-lorry, and a young general. "After that, a Government office, and several enjoyable tea parties—until I was combed out at last. Since then I've been looking for a job. Now—your turn."

comments.note: This refers to staying at the hostel which hasn't been previously introduced.
comments.author: Tom
comments.paragraph: They put down the cups and laughed rather uncertainly. Tuppence rose. "I must return to my palatial suite at the hostel."
